tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': path to the built .app bundle (e.g. DerivedData/.../Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. ## 1a59c906-04da-521d-bda7-7f71b9f9e01c
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai .../artifact/... link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{...}},"markdown":"# <title>

<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

The Rapier user guide pages only describe the API: each rigid body has a linear damping coefficient that affects linear velocity, and the default is 0.0, meaning no damping. Larger values of the damping coefficients lead to a stronger slow-downs. None of the Rapier results state how the coefficient is applied per timestep, so the `1 / (1 + dt·damping)` form you mention is unconfirmed for Rapier.

The formula you're describing matches Unity's 2D documentation. It says linearVelocity *= 1.0f / ( 1.0f + simulation-time-step * linearDamping ). Unity's 3D documentation gives a different form, linearVelocity *= ( 1 - linearDamping * dt ). So the two Unity APIs don't share one formula, and the Rapier implementation may follow either pattern or a third one.

To confirm Rapier's exact behavior, the Rapier source is the best check. The relevant code is in the rigid body integration step (`rapier` crate, under the dynamics module), where the damping is applied to velocity during integration.

content.content:
**Ray-casting** (`World` class)

- **`castRay`** returns the first collider hit, or `null`: `let hit = world.castRay(ray, maxToi, solid);`. The hit point is `ray.pointAt(hit.timeOfImpact)`.
- **`castRayAndGetNormal`** works like `castRay` but also returns the surface normal at the hit: `let hitWithNormal = world.castRayAndGetNormal(ray, maxToi, solid);`
- **`intersectionsWithRay`** calls a callback for each collider the ray hits: `world.intersectionsWithRay(ray, maxToi, solid, (hit) => {`. Returning `false` from the callback stops the search.
- **Parameters:**
  - `maxToi` limits the ray to the segment from the origin to `origin + dir * maxToi`.
  - `solid` controls what happens when the origin is inside a shape. If `true`, the hit is at the origin (`toi = 0.0`). If `false`, the hit is the first boundary crossing.
  - Filter flags, filter groups, excluded colliders or rigid bodies, and a predicate are covered under query filters below.

**Shape intersection tests**

- **`intersectionsWithShape`** (the page spells it this way, not `intersectionWithShape`) finds colliders whose shapes intersect a given shape: `world.intersectionsWithShape(shapePos, shapeRot, shape, (handle) => {`
- **`collidersWithAabbIntersectingAabb`** is the approximate test. It only checks AABBs, not the actual shapes: `world.collidersWithAabbIntersectingAabb(aabbCenter, aabbHalfExtents, (handle) => {`

**Point projection**

- **`projectPoint`** returns the closest collider to a point, with the projected point and an `isInside` flag: `let proj = world.projectPoint(point, solid);`
- **`intersectionsWithPoint`** calls a callback for every collider containing the point: `world.intersectionsWithPoint(point, (handle) => {`

**Query filters**

Most queries accept optional filtering arguments:
- `flags` excludes colliders by type or parent body type.
- `groups` applies collision group rules.
- `exclude_collider` and `exclude_rigid_body` skip a specific collider or body.
- `predicate` is a custom filter function.

Example from the page:
`let hit = world.castRay(ray, maxToi, solid, filterFlags, filterGroups, null, filterExcludeRigidBody, filterPredicate);`

**Hit point computation:** the hit point is `ray.origin + ray.dir * toi`, which the page writes as `ray.pointAt(hit.timeOfImpact)`.

**Query pipeline update requirement:** the page does not cover this, so I can't say from this content whether or when an update is required.

## Collision and solver groups

- **Bit layout:** Each group setting is a 32-bit value. The high 16 bits hold the membership, and the low 16 bits hold the filter. The page states: "The 16 left-most bits contain the memberships whereas the 16 right-most bits contain the filter."
- **Example:** Membership groups `[0, 2, 3]` and filter group `[2]` pack into `0x000D0004`.
- **Interaction rule:** Collision groups are checked after the broad phase. Contacts are computed only if each collider's membership overlaps the other's filter. The page gives this bit-wise check:

  `((A.collisionGroups() >> 16) & (B.collisionGroups() & 0xffff)) != 0`

  `&& ((B.collisionGroups() >> 16) & (A.collisionGroups() & 0xffff)) != 0`
- **Solver groups:** The same test is applied to solver groups after the narrow phase. It controls whether contact forces are computed. Collision groups are preferred because they skip more work.

JS usage:

```
    /* Set the collision groups and solver groups when the collider is created. */let colliderDesc = RAPIER.ColliderDesc.ball(0.5)    .setCollisionGroups(0x000D0004)    .setSolverGroups(0x00500010);
```

## Sensors

- A sensor does not generate contacts, so it produces no contact forces. It only generates "intersection events" when it starts or stops touching another collider.
- Sensors are typically used to detect when something enters an area.
- Sensors still count toward the mass of their rigid body. The page notes that sensors "_do_ contribute to the mass of a rigid-body they are attached to."

JS usage:

```
    /* Set the collider type when the collider is created. */let colliderDesc = RAPIER.ColliderDesc.ball(0.5)    .setSensor(true);
```

```
    /* Set the collider type after the collider creation. */collider.setSensor(true);
```

## Friction and restitution combine rules

- Each collider has its own friction and restitution coefficient. When two colliders touch, a combine rule merges their two values into one.
- The four rules are Average, Min, Multiply, and Max. The default is Average.
- When two colliders use different rules, the page gives this precedence: "GeometricMean > ClampedSum > Max > Multiply > Min > Average".
- Contact modification can override these rules for finer control.

JS usage:

```

```

## Collider mass properties: density vs. mass

- **Density or mass (automatic):** Give the collider a non-zero density (default 1.0) or a non-zero mass. The engine then computes the other properties, such as angular inertia, from the shape. The page recommends this approach.
- **Explicit (manual):** Set the mass and angular inertia directly. This suits real-world objects whose properties are already known.
- **Replacement:** Each of the density, mass, and mass-properties setters replaces whatever the others previously set. The rigid body's mass properties are then updated at the next simulation step, or immediately by calling `RigidBody.recomputeMassPropertiesFromColliders`.

JS usage:

```
let colliderDesc = RAPIER.ColliderDesc.cuboid(1.0, 2.0)    .setDensity(2.0);
```

```
let colliderDesc2 = RAPIER.ColliderDesc.cuboid(1.0, 2.0)    .setMass(0.8);
```

```
let colliderDesc3 = RAPIER.ColliderDesc.cuboid(1.0, 2.0)    .setMassProperties(0.5, { x: 0.0, y: 1.0 }, 0.3);
```

## Active collision types

- By default, collision detection is disabled between two colliders when both are attached to non-dynamic bodies.
- To enable it for a pair such as kinematic and fixed bodies, change the collider's active collision types.
- The page's example enables the default types together with `KINEMATIC_FIXED`.

JS usage:

```

```

## Can a rigid body have several colliders?

Yes. The page describes attaching "one or multiple colliders to a rigid body," which lets the body be affected by contact forces from each of them. Each collider's mass properties are added to the body's total, and each can have its own shape, friction, restitution, and groups.

The final loop uses an accumulator to decouple the physics step from the render rate:

- **Frame time:** Each frame, the loop measures elapsed time and clamps it to 0.25 seconds, so a long stall can't flood the accumulator.
- **Fixed steps:** The elapsed time is added to the accumulator. While the accumulator holds at least one fixed dt, the simulation advances by exactly dt. Before each step, the previous state is saved, and dt is subtracted from the accumulator.
- **Interpolation:** The leftover accumulator value shows how far the render time sits between the last two physics steps. Dividing it by dt gives a blend factor, which is used to mix the previous and current states before rendering. This smooths out the stutter that unsimulated remainder time would otherwise cause.

# Physics: 2D boat physics with Rapier 2D 0.21 and custom projectiles

Target files: `src/sim/physics.ts`, `src/sim/coords.ts`, `src/sim/geom.ts`, `src/sim/boat.ts`, `src/sim/walls.ts`, `src/sim/items.ts`, `src/sim/projectiles.ts`, `src/sim/loop.ts`, `src/sim/sim.ts`, the `PHYSICS` block of `shared/config.ts`, and `tests/sim/*.test.ts`.

Everything below was verified against the installed packages (`@dimforge/rapier2d-compat` 0.21.0, `three` 0.186.1, vite 8.3.4, vitest 5.0.5, TypeScript 5.9, node 24.15): every API name was read from `node_modules/@dimforge/rapier2d-compat/dist/**/*.d.ts`, and every code file in section 3 was typechecked with the repo's `tsconfig.json` options (strict, `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`, plus `noUnusedLocals`/`noUnusedParameters`) and exercised by the 34 vitest tests in section 5, all green, in a scratch mirror of the repo (`scratchpad/research/physics/repo`). Numbers quoted as "measured" come from the proof scripts `proof1.mjs` to `proof5.mjs` in the same folder.

---

## 1. The problem, in the words of the spec

From SPEC.md section 8 (Physics):

- "Gameplay physics runs in 2D on the water plane, and everything is drawn in 3D. Boats never leave the water, so a 2D solver gives correct collisions with far less code and far fewer bugs."
- "Engine: Rapier 2D (WASM build) for boats, walls, poles, crates and mines."
- "Projectiles: small custom code (position, velocity, gravity) with distance checks against boats. Cannonballs and mortar shells arc in 3D; only their impact point matters for hits."
- "Timestep: fixed 60 Hz simulation; the renderer interpolates between steps."
- Boat handling: "Rigid body shaped like a gondola, about 6 m × 1.4 m. GAS pushes forward; reverse is 40% of forward thrust. Strong sideways drag (the keel), so the boat goes where it points. Sideways drag drops during a drift turn, so the stern slides out. Linear and angular damping act as water resistance. Steering strength grows with speed, with a slow turn still possible at rest. Top speed about 10 m/s, 16 m/s with Boost."
- Collisions: "Boat against wall: bounce and scrape sparks, no damage. Boat against boat: both bounce with real momentum exchange. A boosted ram sinks the target; two boosted boats just bounce. A lethal hit applies an impulse at the impact point, so the boat flips and spins as it sinks. The Water Cannon applies a continuous push along its stream. Crates and mines are light bodies that drift and can be shoved around."
- "Visual-only motion (costs nothing in the simulation): boats bob on the waves, roll up to 8° into turns, pitch when accelerating and sit lower when the hull holds water."

Related rules the physics must serve: section 5 ("On a lethal hit the boat flips and sinks (about 2 s)... After 5 s the boat respawns at a random dock... 3 s of spawn protection... Speed is multiplied by 1 − 0.5 × water / 100"), section 6 (Cannon, Torpedo "locks the nearest enemy in a 40° cone ahead and homes along the water", Mortar "auto-ranged lob: lands on the nearest enemy within 10° of the aim line and 60 m, even behind buildings; with no target it lands 40 m ahead. 6 m splash", Mine "arms after 1 s, sinks the first enemy that touches it", crates "respawn 8 s later"), section 7 ("one ASCII grid in shared/map.ts, 8 m per cell... Physics builds its walls from the grid... Coordinates: metres, Y up, water surface at y = 0, map origin at the centre. The 2D physics uses (x, z) of the 3D world.") and section 4 ("In code, aim is just an angle in the 2D top-down simulation: hits are 2D rays and 2D projectile checks.").

The hard parts the spec flags or implies: binding the 2D solver to the 3D scene without sign bugs, making a Rapier body feel like an arcade boat (keel, drift, speed caps), telling a lethal ram from a scrape, keeping a sunk hull in the world without it colliding, building a few dozen wall colliders out of ~1900 map cells, and custom projectiles that respect walls but do not cost a Rapier body each.

---

## 2. Decisions, why, and what was rejected

| # | Decision | Why | Rejected |
|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | `import RAPIER from '@dimforge/rapier2d-compat'` and `await RAPIER.init()` once, loaded with a dynamic `import()` on the SCENE route only. No Vite plugin or config. | The compat bundle inlines the wasm as base64 (`"AGFzbQ..."` decoded by base64-js inside `init()`), so there is no `.wasm` asset for the bundler to handle. Verified: `vite build` of a test app produced `rapier-*.js` 3.4 MB (1.3 MB gzip) with zero config, and the dev server pre-bundled it as `/node_modules/.vite/deps/@dimforge_rapier2d-compat.js`. The dynamic import keeps the 1.3 MB off the phones. | `@dimforge/rapier2d` (needs wasm asset handling and top-level await plugins, the exact thing the spec avoids). `vite-plugin-wasm`: not needed. |
| D2 | Coordinates: `sim.x = world.x`, `sim.y = -world.z`, `simAngle === Object3D.rotation.y`, bow = body local `+y`, forward = `(-sin a, cos a)`. | The mirror `y := -z` preserves handedness, so a positive Rapier angular velocity is a positive Three.js yaw (CCW seen from above). No sign flips anywhere; `rotation.y = body.rotation()`. Pinned by a test that compares with Three's own `applyQuaternion`. | `y := z`: then `yaw = -angle - PI/2` and every angular quantity flips sign; a classic source of "left turns right" bugs. |
| D3 | Boat = dynamic body, `roundCuboid(0.55, 2.85, 0.15)` (effective 0.7 × 3.0 half extents), `setMass(1000)`, `linearDamping 1.0`, `angularDamping 3.0`, `canSleep(false)`. Thrust derived: `F = m·d·v_top = 10 000 N`. | Rapier damping is `v *= 1/(1 + dt·d)` per step (source + measured), so with a constant force the terminal speed is exactly `F/(m·d)` and the approach is `v(t) ≈ v_top(1 − e^{−d t})`: 95 % at 3 s with `d = 1` (measured 9.49 m/s at 3 s). Boost ×1.6 and hull water `×(1 − 0.5·w/100)` scale the thrust and therefore the top speed with no extra clamp. Rounded corners slide over seams between merged wall rectangles. | Mass by density (needs density ≈ 119 for 1000 kg; opaque). `convexHull` of a gondola outline (verified it works: `ShapeType.ConvexPolygon`, inertia 2194 vs 3163 for the box) but the projectile OBB tests would no longer match the hull; adopt it later only if the pointed bow matters for wall scraping. CCD: unnecessary, 16 m/s × 1/60 = 0.27 m per step against 8 m thick walls. |
| D4 | Keel = scale the lateral velocity component each step with `setLinvel`: `v_lat *= exp(−grip·dt)`, `grip = 8 /s` (drift: 1.5 /s). | Exact, monotonic, frame-rate independent, cannot overshoot (measured: lateral 7 → 0.74 m/s after 0.25 s, → 0 by 1 s, no sign change). | Counter impulse `−m·v_lat·k·dt` (also measured stable at 60 Hz, but it is explicit Euler: overshoots if `k·dt > 1`, and the decay then depends on dt). |
| D5 | Steering = torque sized from the steady-state turn rate: `τ = ω_ss · I · angularDamping`, `ω_ss` lerped from 0.5 rad/s at rest to 1.3 rad/s at top speed; angular velocity hard-capped with `setAngvel`. | Angular damping has the same `1/(1+dt·d)` form, so `ω_ss = τ/(I·d)`; the shape-agnostic `body.principalInertia()` makes the torque right for any hull. Time constant `1/d = 0.33 s` feels responsive. Turn radius at top speed `v/ω = 7.7 m`, fits an 8–10 m canal. | Steering by setting angular velocity directly (kills the momentum feel and fights the solver during wall contact). |
| D6 | Ram detection = `COLLISION_EVENTS` "started" between two hulls + the velocities cached just before `world.step` + the contact normal and point from `world.contactPair(...)`. Rammer = boosted, closing speed along the normal ≥ 7 m/s, bow facing the normal (`dot ≥ cos 60°`). Both qualify → bounce. | After the step the solver has already resolved the impact (measured: pre-step 12 m/s, post-step −1.98 m/s), so pre-step velocities are needed. The manifold gives a world-space normal and solver contact point inside the handler (measured on the started event: normal (0,1), point (0.70, 19.00)). | `CONTACT_FORCE_EVENTS` with a threshold: fires in Newtons (solver and mass dependent, measured 50 kN spikes vs 2 kN resting), fires on sustained pushing too, and `TempContactForceEvent` has no contact point. |
| D7 | Sinking: `collider.setCollisionGroups(Masks.boatSinking)` (member SINKING, filter 0) and keep the body dynamic for 2 s, then `body.setEnabled(false)`; respawn = `setEnabled(true)`, `setTranslation`, `setRotation`, `setLinvel(0)`, `setAngvel(0)`, groups → PROTECTED for 3 s, then BOAT. | No body churn (stable handles, stable entity ids, no stale-handle aliasing, see edge case E2). A filter of 0 makes the hull invisible to every pair test and every scene query. | Removing and recreating the body (handle churn). Kinematic body (no drifting while sinking). Separate "ghost" entity. |
| D8 | Lethal-hit impulse: the sim applies `applyImpulseAtPoint(4000 N·s · dir, impactPoint)` so the sinking hull spins and slides in 2D (measured 45 rad/s from a 500 N·s impulse 2.5 m off-centre on a 1000 kg box: scale with care, 4000 N·s at the bow gives about 3.8 rad/s against 3 /s damping). The flip (pitch/roll/submerge) is render-only from `phase === 'sinking'` and `phaseT`. | 2D spin is free and makes the kill-cam read; a 3D flip in the sim would need a 3D solver. | Flip in the sim: no. |
| D9 | Walls: greedy rectangle merge of solid cells into cuboids on one fixed body, plus 4 border slabs; friction 0, restitution 0.4; bridge cells are water; poles are `ball(0.25)`; moored gondolas `cuboid(0.7, 3)` rotated; pile clusters 3 × `ball(0.35)`. | The spec's sample map (8 × 24 cells) merges into 17 rectangles; a 50 × 38 map merges to a few dozen. Zero friction keeps "scrape" from becoming "stick". | One collider per cell (≈ 1000 colliders and a seam at every cell edge). Polyline contours with `PolylineFlags.ORIENTED` (exists in 0.21 and removes corner pushes, but needs contour tracing; keep as the upgrade if hulls still catch on seams). |
| D10 | Crates: dynamic `ball(0.8)`, 20 kg, damping 1.5, `COLLISION_EVENTS`; pickup = the "started" event with a hull; on pickup `setEnabled(false)` and after 8 s teleport home and `setEnabled(true)`. | Solid and light, so a boat with full slots shoves it (spec: "a blue crate is left in the water for someone else") and a boat with a free slot takes it on first touch. No body churn. | Sensor crates (cannot be shoved). Polling with `world.intersectionsWithShape` each step (works, verified; costs one query per boat per step and is only needed for the "slot freed while still touching" corner). |
| D11 | Mines: one dynamic body, two colliders: solid `ball(0.4)` (walls/crates only, so boats pass over it) and a sensor `ball(1.6)` with `density 0`, groups MINE_TRIG ↔ BOAT only; arming after 1 s with a one-off `intersectionPairsWith` poll; 45 s lifetime; deferred body removal. | A sensor never generates forces, so the solid core is what keeps the mine out of walls. Sensors add mass unless density is 0 (measured 17.07 kg vs 10 kg). PROTECTED hulls are not in the sensor's filter, so spawn-protected boats never trigger it. | Sensor only (drifts through walls). |
| D12 | Projectiles are plain objects: cannonball 60 m/s with per-step segment-vs-OBB (box inflated by the ball radius) and `world.castRay(..., Masks.queryWalls)` for walls; torpedo 25 m/s pure pursuit with a 120°/s turn cap, lock in the 40° cone with line of sight, straight when lost; mortar = fixed 1.5 s flight to the target's launch position (no wall check), 6 m splash by point-to-OBB distance; water cannon = 18 m, 12° half-angle cone with line of sight, `addForce` 6 kN along the stream and 25 water/s. | Matches the spec's "2D rays and 2D projectile checks"; a castRay costs 1.2 µs (measured). Own team is skipped everywhere. | Rapier bodies for projectiles (CCD, events, handles for every shot). |
| D13 | Loop: accumulator with `dt = 1/60`, frame clamp 0.25 s, `prev`/`curr` transforms per entity, `alpha = accumulator/dt`; all timers use `simTime`. | Standard "Fix your timestep"; the clamp bounds the catch-up to 15 steps. | Variable timestep (Rapier docs: the step should not vary). |
| D14 | Entity registry = `Map<colliderHandle, EntityRef>`; removals are deferred until the event drain finished. | Handles are opaque f64 numbers (index + generation packed into the bits; measured handles `5e-324`, `1e-323`...), fine as Map keys, never as array indices, and `RigidBody.userData` exists but `Collider` has none while events report collider handles. | `userData` on bodies (typed `unknown`, and events give collider handles anyway). |
| D15 | `phys.commit()` (= one `world.step()`) right after the static world is built. | Scene queries only see a collider after the next step inserts it into the broad phase (measured: `castRay` → null right after `createCollider`, still null after `propagateModifiedBodyPositionsToColliders()`, hit after one step). | Relying on the countdown steps (works in the game, fails in tests and in any "fire on frame 0" harness). |

---

## 3. Algorithms and code

### 3.1 Formulas

- Rapier damping (rapier `src/dynamics/rigid_body_components.rs`, `RigidBodyVelocity::apply_damping`): `linvel *= 1/(1 + dt·linear_damping)`, `angvel *= 1/(1 + dt·angular_damping)`. Measured one-step ratio 0.98360653 = 1/(1 + 1/60).
- Constant force `F` on mass `m` with damping `d`: `v_{n+1} = (v_n + (F/m)·dt) / (1 + dt·d)`; fixed point `v_∞ = F/(m·d)` (measured 10.000 m/s at 10 s with F = 10 000 N, m = 1000, d = 1). Continuous approximation `v(t) = v_∞ (1 − e^{−d t})`: 63 % at 1/d, 95 % at 3/d.
- Same for rotation: `ω_∞ = τ/(I·d_ang)`; the box inertia is `I = m (w² + l²)/12 = 3163 kg·m²` (Rapier reports 3163.333 for `setMass(1000)` on the 0.7 × 3 cuboid).
- Keel: in the body frame `v_f = v·f`, `v_r = v·r` with `f = (−sin a, cos a)`, `r = (cos a, sin a)`; new velocity `f·v_f + r·(v_r·e^{−grip·dt})`.
- Hull water: `thrust *= 1 − 0.5·water/100` → top speed scales identically (measured 5.0 m/s at water 100).
- Ram: with `n` from hull A to hull B, `closing = (v_A − v_B)·n` using the pre-step velocities; A rams if boosted, `closing ≥ 7` and `f_A·n ≥ 0.5`; B rams if boosted, `closing ≥ 7` and `−f_B·n ≥ 0.5`.
- Segment vs OBB: transform the segment into the box frame (`lx = c·dx + s·dy`, `ly = −s·dx + c·dy`), slab test against `±(hw + r)`, `±(hl + r)`, entry `t ∈ [0, 1]`.
- Mortar arc (render only): `s = t/T`, `pos = lerp(launch, landing, s)`, `height = 4·H·s·(1 − s)` with `H = 20 m`, `T = 1.5 s` (a real 9.81 m/s² lob with T = 1.5 s would only rise 2.8 m).
- Cone test: `dist ≤ range` and `|wrap(atan2(−dx, dy) − aim)| ≤ halfAngle`.

---

## 4. Edge cases and how they are handled

- **E1 Queries do not see new colliders until a step.** `castRay`/`intersectionsWithShape` return nothing for a collider created since the last `world.step()`; `propagateModifiedBodyPositionsToColliders()` only refreshes moved colliders. `buildStaticWorld` ends with `phys.commit()`. Mid-game bodies (crates, mines) are never ray targets, and hull hits use our own OBB test, so nothing else depends on it.
- **E2 Stale handles alias.** The JS-side `Coarena` ignores the generation bits: after `removeRigidBody`, `world.colliders.get(staleHandle)` returns `null` until a new collider reuses the slot, then it returns the *new* collider and `contains()` is true again (measured). `PhysicsWorld.removeBody` deletes the registry entries immediately and defers the actual removal until the event drain is over; code never stores raw handles, only `Boat`/`Crate`/`Mine` objects, and `collider.isValid()` is the safe check for a kept wrapper.
- **E3 Handles are not integers.** Collider/body handles beyond index 0 are denormal-looking f64s (`5e-324` = index 1, generation 0). `Map` keys only; no `handles[]` arrays, no `Number.isInteger` checks.
- **E4 Forces persist.** `addForce` accumulates until `resetForces`; `applyBoatControls` resets forces and torques every step, so a disconnected phone (no input) leaves no ghost thrust.
- **E5 NaN from the network.** A `NaN` steer would poison the body for the rest of the match; `applyBoatControls` sanitises with `Number.isFinite`. Do the same for `dYaw` on the gunner side before it reaches the sim.
- **E6 Teleport vs interpolation.** `respawnBoat` and the crate respawn set `prev = curr` to the new pose; otherwise the renderer would slide the hull across the map for one frame.
- **E7 Two lethal events in one step** (torpedo hit and ram, or two torpedoes): `sinkBoat` is a no-op unless `phase === 'alive'`; rules must credit only the first.
- **E8 Hull already inside a sensor when it arms.** No new "started" event would fire; `updateMines` polls `intersectionPairsWith` once at the arming instant (test: mine dropped under an enemy explodes at t = 1 s).
- **E9 Owner over own mine, protected hull over a mine.** Owner is filtered by team in `mineShouldExplode`; protected hulls are not in the sensor's filter at all, so no event is generated.
- **E10 Mine dropped into a wall.** The solid core is 1 m inside an 8 m slab at worst (4 m behind a hull whose stern touches the wall); the solver pushes it back toward the nearest face, which is the water side.
- **E11 Sensor mass.** Sensors contribute mass unless `setDensity(0)`; the mine sensor has density 0 (measured 10.0 kg total).
- **E12 Projectile origin inside a wall.** Shots start at the hull centre, which is always ≥ 0.7 m from any wall; with `solid = true` a ray starting inside a wall would otherwise return t = 0 and splash on the muzzle.
- **E13 Teammate in the line of fire.** Projectile tests skip `team === shooterTeam`; the water cannon skips teammates too (spec: never hurts your own team).
- **E14 Sinking or dead hulls** are `hittable = false` for projectiles and have no collision pairs (filter 0 / body disabled), so torpedoes lose the lock (`!target.hittable`) and run straight.
- **E15 Torpedo lock behind a wall or behind the torpedo.** Lock needs line of sight at launch; it is dropped when the target is > 90° off the torpedo's heading, out of 1.22 × lock range, or the ray to it is blocked; Smoke calls `breakLocks(targetId)`.
- **E16 Mortar with no enemy in the cone** lands 40 m ahead; splash uses point-to-OBB distance, so a hull edge 5.5 m away is hit and 6.5 m away is not (tested).
- **E17 Ram on a glancing or sideways contact.** The bow test (`dot(forward, normal) ≥ 0.5`) and the 7 m/s closing-speed threshold reject scrapes; the resting target gets the closing speed from the rammer's cached velocity, not from post-solver values.
- **E18 Contact without a manifold.** `contactInfo` can return false on the very first event in exotic cases; `detectRam` falls back to the centre-to-centre normal and midpoint.
- **E19 Spiral of death / tab hidden.** Frame time is clamped to 0.25 s (15 steps); the sim clock then lags wall time by design. `requestAnimationFrame` stops in a hidden tab, so the scene PC must keep the tab visible (it does, it is the projector).
- **E20 Wall seams.** Merged rectangles still meet at edges; the rounded hull corners (0.15 m) and zero wall friction stop hulls from catching. If they still do, switch walls to `polyline` contours with `PolylineFlags.ORIENTED`.
- **E21 Sleeping.** Hulls never sleep (`canSleep(false)`); crates and mines may, and a sleeping crate still produces the "started" event when an awake hull touches it (tested).
- **E22 Hull water and reverse.** The water multiplier scales thrust (forward and reverse); the brake force is unscaled so a flooded boat still stops.
- **E23 Steering while reversing** is not inverted (tunable at the playtest).
- **E24 Map border.** Four slabs outside the grid stop boats leaving even where the lagoon reaches the edge.
- **E25 Performance.** Measured 0.13 ms wall time per step for 6 hulls, 24 crates, 6 mines and 100 wall cuboids (Rapier's own `timingStep` 0.013 ms), 1.2 µs per `castRay`: the whole sim is far below 1 ms per frame.
- **E26 Memory.** `EventQueue(true)` auto-drains; `PhysicsWorld.free()` frees the queue and the world on teardown; for a rematch keep the world and respawn.

**Without phones (vitest, `npm run test`)**: the six files below run in ~0.6 s in node; `initPhysics()` in `beforeAll` is all a test needs.

- `tests/sim/coords.test.ts`: heading 0 moves along −z; `rotation.y = simAngle` agrees with Three's own quaternion for five yaws; positive angle = CCW; cell (0,0) is the north-west corner.
- `tests/sim/boat.test.ts`: 95 % of 10 m/s within 3 s and 10.0 at 8 s; boost 16; full hull 5; reverse −4; brake to < 0.6 m/s in 1 s; keel decays lateral velocity monotonically to < 0.05 m/s in 1 s; steer +1 gives negative angular velocity, 0.5 rad/s at rest, more at speed, never above the cap; drift slides and bleeds speed; sink → groups SINKING → disabled after 2 s → respawn protected at the dock → BOAT after 3 s.
- `tests/sim/ram.test.ts`: boosted rammer vs resting enemy from behind → one ram with normal (0,1) and an impact point between the hulls; two boosted head-on → no ram, separated after; unboosted → bounce with momentum exchange (the resting boat is pushed > 0.5 m); slow boosted touch → no ram.
- `tests/sim/walls.test.ts`: 3 × 3 block → 1 rect; L shape → 2 rects; the spec's sample map is covered exactly once with < 1/3 as many rectangles as cells; a ray from water into a building hits half-way, the open canal row has line of sight, a ray with the wrong group mask hits nothing, the border stops a ray shot off the map.
- `tests/sim/projectiles.test.ts`: slab test values; cannonball hits an enemy 30 m ahead in 0.45 s and never the teammate sitting in the line of fire; blocked by a wall; 4° assist; splash at max range; torpedo locks at 14° off and hits, no lock at 32°, turn capped, lock dropped behind a wall; mortar targets through a wall and lands at 1.5 s, 5.5 m splash hits and 6.5 m does not, apex 20 m at half flight; water cannon pushes 6 kN and adds 25/s only to enemies in the cone with line of sight.
- `tests/sim/items.test.ts`: crate touch event, disabled, back home after 8 s; mine mass 10 kg, owner-safe, enemy sinks on touch, body removed after the drain; mine under an enemy explodes on arming; mine expires at 45 s.

**Without phones, on screen (keyboard harness in `src/scene`)**: map arrow keys / WASD to `sim.setPilotInput` (steer ±1, gas, brake), B toggles `boat.boosted`, 1/2/3 fire cannon/torpedo/mortar along the camera aim, M drops a mine, K sinks the focused boat (`sinkBoat`) to see the sink/respawn cycle, F1 draws `world.debugRender()` (`DebugRenderBuffers.vertices` = 2 floats per vertex, `colors` = 4 per vertex; 5496 floats for the proof scene) as a `THREE.LineSegments` on the water plane through `simToWorldX/Z`, and F2 prints `world.timingStep()` with `profilerEnabled = true`. Drive into a wall at full speed (should bounce, not stick), hold BRAKE while turning at speed (stern slides out), drive a second keyboard boat into the first with boost on (sinks it) and without (bounces).

**With one phone (Gate 1)**: the only physics-specific check is the sign of steer: tilt left must turn the bow left on the TV. If it does not, the bug is in the phone's gravity-angle sign, not in the sim: the sim's convention is pinned by `coords.test.ts` (steer +1 → negative angular velocity → clockwise from above).

# Physics: 2D boat physics with Rapier 2D 0.21 and custom projectiles

Target files: `src/sim/physics.ts`, `src/sim/coords.ts`, `src/sim/geom.ts`, `src/sim/boat.ts`, `src/sim/walls.ts`, `src/sim/items.ts`, `src/sim/projectiles.ts`, `src/sim/loop.ts`, `src/sim/sim.ts`, the `PHYSICS` block of `shared/config.ts`, and `tests/sim/*.test.ts`.

Everything below was verified against the installed packages (`@dimforge/rapier2d-compat` 0.21.0, `three` 0.186.1, vite 8.3.4, vitest 5.0.5, TypeScript 5.9, node 24.15): every API name was read from `node_modules/@dimforge/rapier2d-compat/dist/**/*.d.ts`, and every code file in section 3 was typechecked with the repo's `tsconfig.json` options (strict, `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`, plus `noUnusedLocals`/`noUnusedParameters`) and exercised by the 34 vitest tests in section 5, all green, in a scratch mirror of the repo (`scratchpad/research/physics/repo`). Numbers quoted as "measured" come from the proof scripts `proof1.mjs` to `proof5.mjs` in the same folder.

---

## 1. The problem, in the words of the spec

From SPEC.md section 8 (Physics):

- "Gameplay physics runs in 2D on the water plane, and everything is drawn in 3D. Boats never leave the water, so a 2D solver gives correct collisions with far less code and far fewer bugs."
- "Engine: Rapier 2D (WASM build) for boats, walls, poles, crates and mines."
- "Projectiles: small custom code (position, velocity, gravity) with distance checks against boats. Cannonballs and mortar shells arc in 3D; only their impact point matters for hits."
- "Timestep: fixed 60 Hz simulation; the renderer interpolates between steps."
- Boat handling: "Rigid body shaped like a gondola, about 6 m × 1.4 m. GAS pushes forward; reverse is 40% of forward thrust. Strong sideways drag (the keel), so the boat goes where it points. Sideways drag drops during a drift turn, so the stern slides out. Linear and angular damping act as water resistance. Steering strength grows with speed, with a slow turn still possible at rest. Top speed about 10 m/s, 16 m/s with Boost."
- Collisions: "Boat against wall: bounce and scrape sparks, no damage. Boat against boat: both bounce with real momentum exchange. A boosted ram sinks the target; two boosted boats just bounce. A lethal hit applies an impulse at the impact point, so the boat flips and spins as it sinks. The Water Cannon applies a continuous push along its stream. Crates and mines are light bodies that drift and can be shoved around."
- "Visual-only motion (costs nothing in the simulation): boats bob on the waves, roll up to 8° into turns, pitch when accelerating and sit lower when the hull holds water."

Related rules the physics must serve: section 5 ("On a lethal hit the boat flips and sinks (about 2 s)... After 5 s the boat respawns at a random dock... 3 s of spawn protection... Speed is multiplied by 1 − 0.5 × water / 100"), section 6 (Cannon, Torpedo "locks the nearest enemy in a 40° cone ahead and homes along the water", Mortar "auto-ranged lob: lands on the nearest enemy within 10° of the aim line and 60 m, even behind buildings; with no target it lands 40 m ahead. 6 m splash", Mine "arms after 1 s, sinks the first enemy that touches it", crates "respawn 8 s later"), section 7 ("one ASCII grid in shared/map.ts, 8 m per cell... Physics builds its walls from the grid... Coordinates: metres, Y up, water surface at y = 0, map origin at the centre. The 2D physics uses (x, z) of the 3D world.") and section 4 ("In code, aim is just an angle in the 2D top-down simulation: hits are 2D rays and 2D projectile checks.").

The hard parts the spec flags or implies: binding the 2D solver to the 3D scene without sign bugs, making a Rapier body feel like an arcade boat (keel, drift, speed caps), telling a lethal ram from a scrape, keeping a sunk hull in the world without it colliding, building a few dozen wall colliders out of ~1900 map cells, and custom projectiles that respect walls but do not cost a Rapier body each.

---

## 2. Decisions, why, and what was rejected

| # | Decision | Why | Rejected |
|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | `import RAPIER from '@dimforge/rapier2d-compat'` and `await RAPIER.init()` once, loaded with a dynamic `import()` on the SCENE route only. No Vite plugin or config. | The compat bundle inlines the wasm as base64 (`"AGFzbQ..."` decoded by base64-js inside `init()`), so there is no `.wasm` asset for the bundler to handle. Verified: `vite build` of a test app produced `rapier-*.js` 3.4 MB (1.3 MB gzip) with zero config, and the dev server pre-bundled it as `/node_modules/.vite/deps/@dimforge_rapier2d-compat.js`. The dynamic import keeps the 1.3 MB off the phones. | `@dimforge/rapier2d` (needs wasm asset handling and top-level await plugins, the exact thing the spec avoids). `vite-plugin-wasm`: not needed. |
| D2 | Coordinates: `sim.x = world.x`, `sim.y = -world.z`, `simAngle === Object3D.rotation.y`, bow = body local `+y`, forward = `(-sin a, cos a)`. | The mirror `y := -z` preserves handedness, so a positive Rapier angular velocity is a positive Three.js yaw (CCW seen from above). No sign flips anywhere; `rotation.y = body.rotation()`. Pinned by a test that compares with Three's own `applyQuaternion`. | `y := z`: then `yaw = -angle - PI/2` and every angular quantity flips sign; a classic source of "left turns right" bugs. |
| D3 | Boat = dynamic body, `roundCuboid(0.55, 2.85, 0.15)` (effective 0.7 × 3.0 half extents), `setMass(1000)`, `linearDamping 1.0`, `angularDamping 3.0`, `canSleep(false)`. Thrust derived: `F = m·d·v_top = 10 000 N`. | Rapier damping is `v *= 1/(1 + dt·d)` per step (source + measured), so with a constant force the terminal speed is exactly `F/(m·d)` and the approach is `v(t) ≈ v_top(1 − e^{−d t})`: 95 % at 3 s with `d = 1` (measured 9.49 m/s at 3 s). Boost ×1.6 and hull water `×(1 − 0.5·w/100)` scale the thrust and therefore the top speed with no extra clamp. Time constant `1/d = 0.33 s` feels responsive. Turn radius at top speed `v/ω = 7.7 m`, fits an 8–10 m canal. | Steering by setting angular velocity directly (kills the momentum feel and fights the solver during wall contact). |
| D6 | Ram detection = `COLLISION_EVENTS` "started" between two hulls + the velocities cached just before `world.step` + the contact normal and point from `world.contactPair(...)`. Rammer = boosted, closing speed along the normal ≥ 7 m/s, bow facing the normal (`dot ≥ cos 60°`). Both qualify → bounce. | After the step the solver has already resolved the impact (measured: pre-step 12 m/s, post-step −1.98 m/s), so pre-step velocities are needed. A filter of 0 makes the hull invisible to every pair test and every scene query. | Removing and recreating the body (handle churn). Kinematic body (no drifting while sinking). The flip (pitch/roll/submerge) is render-only from `phase === 'sinking'` and `phaseT`. | 2D spin is free and makes the kill-cam read; a 3D flip in the sim would need a 3D solver. | Flip in the sim: no. |

Zero friction keeps "scrape" from becoming "stick". | One collider per cell (≈ 1000 colliders and a seam at every cell edge). Polyline contours with `PolylineFlags.ORIENTED` (exists in 0.21 and removes corner pushes, but needs contour tracing; keep as the upgrade if hulls still catch on seams). |

---

## 3. Algorithms and code

### 3.1 Formulas

- Rapier damping (rapier `src/dynamics/rigid_body_components.rs`, `RigidBodyVelocity::apply_damping`): `linvel *= 1/(1 + dt·linear_damping)`, `angvel *= 1/(1 + dt·angular_damping)`. Measured one-step ratio 0.98360653 = 1/(1 + 1/60).
- Constant force `F` on mass `m` with damping `d`: `v_{n+1} = (v_n + (F/m)·dt) / (1 + dt·d)`; fixed point `v_∞ = F/(m·d)` (measured 10.000 m/s at 10 s with F = 10 000 N, m = 1000, d = 1). Continuous approximation `v(t) = v_∞ (1 − e^{−d t})`: 63 % at 1/d, 95 % at 3/d.
- Same for rotation: `ω_∞ = τ/(I·d_ang)`; the box inertia is `I = m (w² + l²)/12 = 3163 kg·m²` (Rapier reports 3163.333 for `setMass(1000)` on the 0.7 × 3 cuboid).
- Keel: in the body frame `v_f = v·f`, `v_r = v·r` with `f = (−sin a, cos a)`, `r = (cos a, sin a)`; new velocity `f·v_f + r·(v_r·e^{−grip·dt})`.
- Hull water: `thrust *= 1 − 0.5·water/100` → top speed scales identically (measured 5.0 m/s at water 100).
- Ram: with `n` from hull A to hull B, `closing = (v_A − v_B)·n` using the pre-step velocities; A rams if boosted, `closing ≥ 7` and `f_A·n ≥ 0.5`; B rams if boosted, `closing ≥ 7` and `−f_B·n ≥ 0.5`.
- Segment vs OBB: transform the segment into the box frame (`lx = c·dx + s·dy`, `ly = −s·dx + c·dy`), slab test against `±(hw + r)`, `±(hl + r)`, entry `t ∈ [0, 1]`.
- Mortar arc (render only): `s = t/T`, `pos = lerp(launch, landing, s)`, `height = 4·H·s·(1 − s)` with `H = 20 m`, `T = 1.5 s` (a real 9.81 m/s² lob with T = 1.5 s would only rise 2.8 m).

## 4. Edge cases and how they are handled

- **E1 Queries do not see new colliders until a step.** `castRay`/`intersectionsWithShape` return nothing for a collider created since the last `world.step()`; `propagateModifiedBodyPositionsToColliders()` only refreshes moved colliders. `buildStaticWorld` ends with `phys.commit()`. Mid-game bodies (crates, mines) are never ray targets, and hull hits use our own OBB test, so nothing else depends on it.
- **E2 Stale handles alias.** The JS-side `Coarena` ignores the generation bits: after `removeRigidBody`, `world.colliders.get(staleHandle)` returns `null` until a new collider reuses the slot, then it returns the *new* collider and `contains()` is true again (measured). `PhysicsWorld.removeBody` deletes the registry entries immediately and defers the actual removal until the event drain is over; code never stores raw handles, only `Boat`/`Crate`/`Mine` objects, and `collider.isValid()` is the safe check for a kept wrapper.
- **E3 Handles are not integers.** Collider/body handles beyond index 0 are denormal-looking f64s (`5e-324` = index 1, generation 0). `Map` keys only; no `handles[]` arrays, no `Number.isInteger` checks.
- **E4 Forces persist.** `addForce` accumulates until `resetForces`; `applyBoatControls` resets forces and torques every step, so a disconnected phone (no input) leaves no ghost thrust.
- **E5 NaN from the network.** A `NaN` steer would poison the body for the rest of the match; `applyBoatControls` sanitises with `Number.isFinite`. Do the same for `dYaw` on the gunner side before it reaches the sim.
- **E6 Teleport vs interpolation.** `respawnBoat` and the crate respawn set `prev = curr` to the new pose; otherwise the renderer would slide the hull across the map for one frame.
- **E7 Two lethal events in one step** (torpedo hit and ram, or two torpedoes): `sinkBoat` is a no-op unless `phase === 'alive'`; rules must credit only the first.
- **E8 Hull already inside a sensor when it arms.** No new "started" event would fire; `updateMines` polls `intersectionPairsWith` once at the arming instant (test: mine dropped under an enemy explodes at t = 1 s).
- **E9 Owner over own mine, protected hull over a mine.** Owner is filtered by team in `mineShouldExplode`; protected hulls are not in the sensor's filter at all, so no event is generated.
- **E10 Mine dropped into a wall.** The solid core is 1 m inside an 8 m slab at worst (4 m behind a hull whose stern touches the wall); the solver pushes it back toward the nearest face, which is the water side.
- **E11 Sensor mass.** Sensors contribute mass unless `setDensity(0)`; the mine sensor has density 0 (measured 10.0 kg total).
- **E12 Projectile origin inside a wall.** Shots start at the hull centre, which is always ≥ 0.7 m from any wall; with `solid = true` a ray starting inside a wall would otherwise return t = 0 and splash on the muzzle.
- **E13 Teammate in the line of fire.** Projectile tests skip `team === shooterTeam`; the water cannon skips teammates too (spec: never hurts your own team).
- **E14 Sinking or dead hulls** are `hittable = false` for projectiles and have no collision pairs (filter 0 / body disabled), so torpedoes lose the lock (`!target.hittable`) and run straight.
- **E15 Torpedo lock behind a wall or behind the torpedo.** Lock needs line of sight at launch; it is dropped when the target is > 90° off the torpedo's heading, out of 1.22 × lock range, or the ray to it is blocked; Smoke calls `breakLocks(targetId)`.
- **E16 Mortar with no enemy in the cone** lands 40 m ahead; splash uses point-to-OBB distance, so a hull edge 5.5 m away is hit and 6.5 m away is not (tested).
- **E17 Ram on a glancing or sideways contact.** The bow test (`dot(forward, normal) ≥ 0.5`) and the 7 m/s closing-speed threshold reject scrapes; the resting target gets the closing speed from the rammer's cached velocity, not from post-solver values.
- **E18 Contact without a manifold.** `contactInfo` can return false on the very first event in exotic cases; `detectRam` falls back to the centre-to-centre normal and midpoint.
- **E19 Spiral of death / tab hidden.** Frame time is clamped to 0.25 s (15 steps); the sim clock then lags wall time by design. `requestAnimationFrame` stops in a hidden tab, so the scene PC must keep the tab visible (it does, it is the projector).
- **E20 Wall seams.** Merged rectangles still meet at edges; the rounded hull corners (0.15 m) and zero wall friction stop hulls from catching. If they still do, switch walls to `polyline` contours with `PolylineFlags.ORIENTED`.
- **E21 Sleeping.** Hulls never sleep (`canSleep(false)`); crates and mines may, and a sleeping crate still produces the "started" event when an awake hull touches it (tested).
- **E22 Hull water and reverse.** The water multiplier scales thrust (forward and reverse); the brake force is unscaled so a flooded boat still stops.
- **E23 Steering while reversing** is not inverted (tunable at the playtest).
- **E24 Map border.** Four slabs outside the grid stop boats leaving even where the lagoon reaches the edge.
- **E25 Performance.** Measured 0.13 ms wall time per step for 6 hulls, 24 crates, 6 mines and 100 wall cuboids (Rapier's own `timingStep` 0.013 ms), 1.2 µs per `castRay`: the whole sim is far below 1 ms per frame.
- **E26 Memory.** `EventQueue(true)` auto-drains; `PhysicsWorld.free()` frees the queue and the world on teardown; for a rematch keep the world and respawn.

## 5. How to test on day one

**Without phones (vitest, `npm run test`)**: the six files below run in ~0.6 s in node; `initPhysics()` in `beforeAll` is all a test needs.

- `tests/sim/coords.test.ts`: heading 0 moves along −z; `rotation.y = simAngle` agrees with Three's own quaternion for five yaws; positive angle = CCW; cell (0,0) is the north-west corner.

- `tests/sim/ram.test.ts`: boosted rammer vs resting enemy from behind → one ram with normal (0,1) and an impact point between the hulls; two boosted head-on → no ram, separated after; unboosted → bounce with momentum exchange (the resting boat is pushed > 0.5 m); slow boosted touch → no ram.
- `tests/sim/walls.test.ts`: 3 × 3 block → 1 rect; L shape → 2 rects; the spec's sample map is covered exactly once with < 1/3 as many rectangles as cells; a ray from water into a building hits half-way, the open canal row has line of sight, a ray with the wrong group mask hits nothing, the border stops a ray shot off the map.
- `tests/sim/projectiles.test.ts`: slab test values; cannonball hits an enemy 30 m ahead in 0.45 s and never the teammate sitting in the line of fire; blocked by a wall; 4° assist; splash at max range; torpedo locks at 14° off and hits, no lock at 32°, turn capped, lock dropped behind a wall; mortar targets through a wall and lands at 1.5 s, 5.5 m splash hits and 6.5 m does not, apex 20 m at half flight; water cannon pushes 6 kN and adds 25/s only to enemies in the cone with line of sight.
- `tests/sim/items.test.ts`: crate touch event, disabled, back home after 8 s; mine mass 10 kg, owner-safe, enemy sinks on touch, body removed after the drain; mine under an enemy explodes on arming; mine expires at 45 s.

**Without phones, on screen (keyboard harness in `src/scene`)**: map arrow keys / WASD to `sim.setPilotInput` (steer ±1, gas, brake), B toggles `boat.boosted`, 1/2/3 fire cannon/torpedo/mortar along the camera aim, M drops a mine, K sinks the focused boat (`sinkBoat`) to see the sink/respawn cycle, F1 draws `world.debugRender()` (`DebugRenderBuffers.vertices` = 2 floats per vertex, `colors` = 4 per vertex; 5496 floats for the proof scene) as a `THREE.LineSegments` on the water plane through `simToWorldX/Z`, and F2 prints `world.timingStep()` with `profilerEnabled = true`. input.summary: Researched and prototyped the whole physics layer for Gondola Royale against the installed packages. Every Rapier API claim was read from node_modules/@dimforge/rapier2d-compat/dist/**/*.d.ts and proven with node scripts (init, stepping, events, contactPair, castRay with group filters, handles, removal, query visibility, timings). The deliverable final.md (122 KB) contains: the spec's problem statement; 15 decisions with rejected alternatives; formulas (Rapier damping v*=1/(1+dt*d), terminal speed F/(m d), steering torque from the steady-state rate, keel decay, ram closing speed, slab test, mortar parabola); nine ready-to-paste TypeScript files plus the PHYSICS config block, all typechecked with the repo's strict tsconfig (plus noUnusedLocals/Parameters) in a scratch mirror; 26 edge cases with their handling; a day-one test plan with and without phones; six passing vitest files (34 tests) embedded as Appendix B; sources; and an appendix of measured numbers. Key findings a skeptic should know: (1) coordinate binding sim.y = -world.z with the bow as Rapier local +y makes simAngle identical to Object3D.rotation.y and keeps angular-velocity signs (pinned by a test against Three's own quaternion); (2) Rapier 2D 0.21 collider/body handles are opaque f64 numbers whose JS-side lookup ignores the generation, so stale handles alias newer colliders in the same slot: the design keys a Map by handle and defers removals; (3) scene queries see a new collider only after the next world.step() (propagateModifiedBodyPositionsToColliders does not help), so the static world build ends with one step; (4) sensors add mass unless density 0; (5) the compat bundle needs zero Vite config (verified vite build and dev pre-bundling), 3.4 MB / 1.3 MB gzip, loaded by dynamic import on the SCENE route only; (6) step cost is 0.13 ms for a full scene, castRay 1.2 microseconds. Thrust 10 kN with linear damping 1.0 on a 1000 kg hull gives exactly 10 m/s top speed (95 % at 3 s), boost x1.6 gives 16 m/s, hull water scales thrust. Rams are detected from collision 'started' events using velocities cached before the step plus the manifold normal and solver contact point; sinking hulls switch collision groups to a zero filter, are disabled after 2 s, and are teleported and protected on respawn.

decisions.decision: Use @dimforge/rapier2d-compat with `await RAPIER.init()` once, loaded by dynamic import on the SCENE route; no Vite plugins or optimizeDeps changes.
decisions.rationale: The compat ESM bundle inlines the wasm as base64 (init = `gC`, decodes `jg.toByteArray("AGFzbQ...")`); a scratch `vite build` produced a 3.4 MB (1.3 MB gzip) rapier chunk with zero config and the dev server pre-bundled it; the dynamic import keeps it off phones.
decisions.alternatives: @dimforge/rapier2d (needs wasm asset + top-level-await handling), vite-plugin-wasm.

decisions.decision: Coordinates: sim.x = world.x, sim.y = -world.z, simAngle === Object3D.rotation.y, bow = Rapier body local +y so forward = (-sin a, cos a).
decisions.rationale: The mirror keeps handedness, so positive Rapier angular velocity is a positive yaw (CCW from above); no sign flips; pinned by a vitest comparing with Three r186 applyQuaternion.
decisions.alternatives: y := z (yaw = -angle - PI/2 and inverted angular signs everywhere).

decisions.decision: Boat = dynamic body, roundCuboid(0.55, 2.85, 0.15) (effective 0.7 x 3.0 half extents), setMass(1000), linearDamping 1.0, angularDamping 3.0, canSleep false, no CCD; thrust derived as m*d*v_top = 10 kN; boost x1.6; hull water multiplies thrust.
decisions.rationale: Rapier damping is v *= 1/(1+dt*d) (source + measured), so terminal speed is exactly F/(m d) and 95 % is reached at 3/d = 3 s (measured 9.49 m/s at 3 s, 10.00 at 10 s); rounded corners slide over wall seams; 0.27 m per step cannot tunnel 8 m walls.
decisions.alternatives: Density-based mass; convexHull gondola outline (verified to work, inertia 2194) rejected for now because projectile OBB tests would no longer match the hull.

decisions.decision: Keel implemented by scaling the lateral velocity component each step with setLinvel: v_lat *= exp(-grip*dt), grip 8/s (1.5/s while drifting).
decisions.rationale: Exact, monotonic, frame-rate independent, cannot overshoot; measured lateral 7 -> 0.74 m/s at 0.25 s and ~0 at 1 s with no sign change.
decisions.alternatives: Counter impulse -m*v_lat*k*dt (also measured stable at 60 Hz but explicit Euler, dt-dependent, overshoots if k*dt > 1).

decisions.decision: Steering torque sized from the steady-state turn rate: tau = omega_ss * I * angularDamping with omega_ss lerped 0.5 -> 1.3 rad/s by speed, drift x1.5, angular velocity capped at 1.8 rad/s via setAngvel.
decisions.rationale: Angular damping has the same 1/(1+dt*d) form so omega_ss = tau/(I d); principalInertia() keeps it shape-agnostic; turn radius 7.7 m at top speed fits 8-10 m canals.
decisions.alternatives: Setting angular velocity directly (loses momentum feel, fights the solver during contacts).

decisions.decision: Ram detection from COLLISION_EVENTS 'started' between hulls, using velocities cached before world.step plus the normal and solver contact point from world.contactPair; rammer must be boosted, closing speed >= 7 m/s and bow facing the normal (dot >= 0.5); both qualifying -> bounce.
decisions.rationale: After the step the solver has already resolved the impact (measured pre-step 12 m/s, post-step -1.98 m/s); the manifold is readable inside the handler on the started event (normal (0,1), point (0.70,19.00)).
decisions.alternatives: CONTACT_FORCE_EVENTS with a Newton threshold (solver/mass dependent, fires on sustained pushing, no contact point in TempContactForceEvent).

decisions.decision: Sinking: collider.setCollisionGroups(SINKING member, filter 0) and keep the body dynamic 2 s with an applyImpulseAtPoint spin, then body.setEnabled(false); respawn = setEnabled(true), setTranslation, setRotation, setLinvel 0, setAngvel 0, groups PROTECTED for 3 s then BOAT; the 3D flip is render-only.
decisions.rationale: No body churn (stable handles and ids, avoids stale-handle aliasing); filter 0 removes the hull from every pair test and scene query; 2D spin is free and sells the kill-cam.
decisions.alternatives: Remove and recreate the body; kinematic body; a 3D flip in the sim.

decisions.decision: Walls: greedy row-major rectangle merge of solid map cells into cuboids on one fixed body, plus 4 border slabs, friction 0, restitution 0.4; bridge cells are water; poles ball(0.25), moored gondolas rotated cuboid(0.7,3), pile clusters 3 x ball(0.35); buildStaticWorld ends with phys.commit() (one world.step).
decisions.rationale: The spec's sample map (101 solid cells) merges into 8 rectangles; zero friction keeps scrapes from sticking; scene queries only see colliders after a step (measured).
decisions.alternatives: One collider per cell (~1000 colliders and seams); polyline contours with PolylineFlags.ORIENTED (kept as the upgrade if hulls catch on seams).

decisions.decision: Crates are solid light dynamic balls (0.8 m, 20 kg, damping 1.5) with COLLISION_EVENTS; pickup = the started event with a hull; collected crates are setEnabled(false) and re-enabled at home after 8 s.
decisions.rationale: A boat with full slots shoves the crate as the spec says, a boat with a free slot takes it on first touch; no body churn (tested).
decisions.alternatives: Sensor crates (cannot be shoved); per-step intersectionsWithShape polling (works, extra query per boat per step).

decisions.decision: Mines are one dynamic body with two colliders: solid ball(0.4) in group MINE_BODY (walls/crates only) and a sensor ball(1.6) with density 0 in MINE_TRIG (filter BOAT only, so PROTECTED hulls never trigger); arm after 1 s with a one-off intersectionPairsWith poll; 45 s lifetime; deferred removal.
decisions.rationale: Sensors generate no forces, so the solid core keeps mines out of walls; sensors add mass unless density 0 (measured 17.07 vs 10 kg); a hull already inside the sensor at arming gets no new started event (tested).
decisions.alternatives: Sensor-only mine (drifts through walls).

decisions.decision: Projectiles are plain objects: cannonball 60 m/s with per-step segment-vs-OBB (box inflated by radius) and world.castRay(ray, 1, true, undefined, Masks.queryWalls) for walls; torpedo 25 m/s pure pursuit, 120 deg/s turn cap, lock in the 40 deg cone with line of sight, straight when lost; mortar fixed 1.5 s flight to the target's launch position with no wall check and 6 m point-to-OBB splash; water cannon 18 m / 12 deg cone with LOS, addForce 6 kN and 25 water/s; own team always skipped; 4 deg aim assist within 10 deg capture.
decisions.rationale: Matches the spec's 2D rays and projectile checks; castRay costs 1.2 us; the two-way group test means query masks use membership 0xffff.
decisions.alternatives: Rapier bodies with CCD for projectiles.

decisions.decision: Fixed-step loop: accumulator, dt 1/60, 0.25 s frame clamp, prev/curr Transform2 per entity, alpha = accumulator/dt, shortest-arc angle lerp, all timers on simTime; snapshots reset on teleports.
decisions.rationale: Fix-your-timestep; clamp bounds catch-up to 15 steps; resetting prev on respawn prevents a one-frame slide across the map.
decisions.alternatives: Variable timestep (Rapier docs advise against varying dt).

decisions.decision: Entity registry is a Map keyed by collider handle with EntityRef {kind, id}; removals are deferred until the event drain finishes; no body/collider userData.
decisions.rationale: Handles are opaque f64 bit-packed values (5e-324 etc.), events report collider handles, Collider has no userData (only RigidBody does), and the JS Coarena ignores generation bits so stale handles alias newer colliders (measured).
decisions.alternatives: RigidBody.userData (typed unknown, bodies not colliders); arrays indexed by handle (impossible).
